message.content:
Yes—**sports can help make a nation**, but mostly by *strengthening national identity* rather than creating a nation from nothing. Research on Africa Cup of Nations and World Cup tournaments found that victories reduced strong ethnic identification, improved attitudes toward other ethnic groups, and reduced inter-ethnic violence, suggesting sports can support nation-building in divided societies.[1]

Sports do this by creating shared symbols, emotions, and public rituals that bring strangers together around a common team or event.[1][2] The effect is strongest when the national team itself is diverse, because victories can signal that different groups can cooperate successfully.[1]

At the same time, sports are not a substitute for politics or institutions. They can open a short-term window for unity, dialogue, or reform, but lasting nation-building still depends on broader social and political change.[1][5]
